req.title: Emit OpenAPI schema
req.statement: The system shall serve an OpenAPI 3.x JSON specification at GET /openapi.json.

doc.reasoning: The requirement mandates that GET /openapi.json returns an HTTP 2xx response with a valid OpenAPI 3.x JSON payload. Tests cover: (1) positive EP — nominal GET returns 200 with correct content-type and OpenAPI structure including exact title/version from app config; (2) negative NEG — wrong HTTP method (POST) returns 405; (3) boundary BVA — schema contains required top-level OpenAPI 3.x keys and the 'paths' key is non-empty, asserting exact key presence to catch mutations that strip or rename fields. Each test uses exact-value assertions to maximise mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_openapi_json_positive_returns_200_with_valid_schema
expected: Response body is valid JSON with key 'openapi' starting with '3.'
Response body contains 'info' with title 'Task Manager API' and version '1.0.0'
trace: R-TASK-019: system shall serve OpenAPI 3.x JSON at GET /openapi.json
tests.executable:
from app.main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

def test_openapi_json_positive_returns_200_with_valid_schema():
    r = client.get("/openapi.json")
    assert r.status_code == 200
    ct = r.headers.get("content-type", "")
    assert "application/json" in ct
    body = r.json()
    assert isinstance(body, dict)
    assert "openapi" in body
    assert body["openapi"].startswith("3.")
    assert "info" in body
    assert body["info"]["title"] == "Task Manager API"
    assert body["info"]["version"] == "1.0.0"
    assert "paths" in body
    assert isinstance(body["paths"], dict)
    assert len(body["paths"]) > 0

tests.name: test_openapi_json_boundary_required_top_level_keys_present
actions: Inspect all required OpenAPI 3.x top-level keys
expected: Keys 'openapi', 'info', 'paths' all present in response body
'openapi' value is exactly '3.1.0' or starts with '3.' (not '2.' Swagger)
trace: R-TASK-019: OpenAPI 3.x specification — boundary on required structural keys
tests.executable:
from app.main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

def test_openapi_json_boundary_required_top_level_keys_present():
    r = client.get("/openapi.json")
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.json()
    for key in ("openapi", "info", "paths"):
        assert key in body, f"Missing top-level key: {key}"
    openapi_ver = body["openapi"]
    assert openapi_ver.startswith("3."), f"Expected OpenAPI 3.x, got {openapi_ver}"
    assert not openapi_ver.startswith("2."), "Got Swagger 2.x, not OpenAPI 3.x"
    info = body["info"]
    assert "title" in info
    assert "version" in info
    assert info["title"] == "Task Manager API"
    assert info["version"] == "1.0.0"
    paths = body["paths"]
    assert "/tasks/" in paths
    assert "/tasks/{task_id}" in paths
    assert "/" in paths

from app.main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

def test_openapi_json_positive_content_type_exact():
    r = client.get("/openapi.json")
    assert r.status_code == 200
    ct = r.headers.get("content-type", "")
    assert "application/json" in ct
    body = r.json()
    assert isinstance(body, dict)
    assert not isinstance(body, list)
    assert "openapi" in body
    assert "info" in body
    assert "paths" in body
    assert body["info"]["description"] == "A simple REST API for managing tasks"

tests.name: test_openapi_json_boundary_paths_contain_all_task_operations
actions: Inspect 'paths' for all expected HTTP methods on task endpoints
trace: R-TASK-019: schema must reflect all registered routes — boundary on operation count
tests.executable:
from app.main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

def test_openapi_json_boundary_paths_contain_all_task_operations():
    r = client.get("/openapi.json")
    assert r.status_code == 200
    paths = r.json()["paths"]
    tasks_collection = paths.get("/tasks/", {})
    assert "get" in tasks_collection
    assert "post" in tasks_collection
    tasks_item = paths.get("/tasks/{task_id}", {})
    assert "get" in tasks_item
    assert "put" in tasks_item
    assert "delete" in tasks_item
    assert len(tasks_collection) >= 2
    assert len(tasks_item) >= 3
